title: Continuous robotic ultrasound hepatectomy versus intermittent robotic ultrasound hepatectomy for parenchyma-sparing liver surgery
summary: Modern liver surgery aims to remove tumors while preserving as much healthy liver tissue as possible. Ultrasound is important to guide the operation but is usually used only at certain times during surgery. We developed a new robotic surgical technique, called CRUSH, that allows continuous ultrasound monitoring throughout the procedure. This trial investigates whether CRUSH improves the accuracy of tumor removal compared to standard intermittent ultrasound use.
conditions: Malignant neoplasm of liver and intrahepatic bile ducts

interventions.name: Robotic parenchyma-sparing hepatectomy using continuous ultrasound monitoring
Robotic parenchyma-sparing hepatectomy with intermittent ultrasound monitoring

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-	Patients undergoing robotic parenchyma-sparing hepatectomy for benign or malignant lesions who meet the following criteria:	
o	non-anatomical or (sub)segmentectomy
o	technically feasible wide resection margin >10mm to liver parenchyma according to preoperative imaging and no planned R1-vascular resection
-	Age equal to or greater than 18 years
-	Written informed consent
-	ASA I-III
Exclusion criteria:
•	Patients requiring major hepatectomy, vascular reconstruction and/or extrahepatic resections
•	Patients during pregnancy and breastfeeding
•	Impaired mental state or language barrier
•	Suspected lack of compliance
